memories.memory_text: I saw Strack's briefcase on his desk and noticed papers sticking out, so I pulled them out and found a confidential memo from Louis Strack Sr. to Claude Belasarious that linked Strack to the fire.

memories.memory_text: I confronted Strack directly, telling him the fire wasn't an accident—that it was him.

memories.memory_text: I was told by Strack that he wouldn't kill me, not out of mercy, but because I have no power to harm him and the police department would be unsympathetic to my claims.

grounded_facts: Strack informs Durant that he failed to eliminate Westlake completely, calling it a loose end.
Strack instructs Durant to finish off Westlake, who survived the previous assassination attempt.
memories.memory_text: I inferred that Strack knew Durant had failed to kill Westlake completely and that he ordered him to finish the job, calling it a loose end.

grounded_facts: Julie exits a cab and begins crossing the street toward the warehouse.
memories.memory_text: I exited the cab and started crossing the street toward the warehouse.

grounded_facts: Trapped and frightened, Julie shouts Peyton's name, likely seeking help.
Julie shouts Peyton's name in fear and desperation after being cornered by two cars.
memories.memory_text: I shouted Peyton's name because I was trapped and scared, hoping he could help me when the two cars cornered me.

grounded_facts: Guzman and Smiley emerge from the two Lincoln Continentals, initiating direct confrontation with Julie.
memories.memory_text: I saw Guzman and Smiley jump out of the two Lincoln Continentals and come toward me, starting a direct confrontation.

grounded_facts: Two Lincoln Continentals suddenly appear and block Julie’s movement, trapping her between them.
memories.memory_text: I was suddenly trapped between two Lincoln Continentals that sped in and blocked my path.

grounded_facts: Julie is forcibly taken and driven away in one of the Continentals' cars.
memories.memory_text: I was forcibly taken and shoved into one of the Continentals' cars before being driven away.

grounded_facts: Strack prepares to push Julie off the girder, declaring it his tragedy to kill those he loves.
memories.memory_text: I recoiled when Strack stepped in front of me, and I felt his hands on my shoulders as he prepared to push me off the girder—he told me it was his tragedy to kill those he loves, and I knew in that moment he meant to kill me.

grounded_facts: Darkman reappears disguised as Strack's father, confronting him just as he prepares to kill Julie.
memories.memory_text: I was trapped on the girder, and Strack was about to kill me, saying it was the tragedy of his life that he always had to kill the ones he loved—then a voice behind him said 'Iduis!' and 'I should've snuffed you out at birth!' in a horrible rasp, and I saw Strack Sr. rip off his own face to reveal Darkman beneath.

grounded_facts: Julie tells Darkman she loves him regardless of his appearance, trying to reconnect emotionally.
memories.memory_text: I told him I love him no matter how he looks, that the burns don't change how I feel about Peyton.

grounded_facts: Darkman reveals his belief that his hands can only destroy now, and that he has changed irreversibly inside.
memories.memory_text: I remember him saying his hands used to caress me, but now they can only destroy, tear things apart.

grounded_facts: Darkman refuses Julie's attempt to comfort and connect, asserting that no one can help him and that he has fundamentally changed inside.
memories.memory_text: I heard him say that no one can help him and that he doesn't think anyone else can live with what he's become now.

grounded_facts: Darkman exits the elevator, dons a mask, and blends into pedestrian traffic, concealing his identity while Julie searches for him.
memories.memory_text: I saw him pull open the elevator, vanish into the shadows, and then a pedestrian appeared on the other side of the construction trailer—I knew it was Darkman, so I chased after him, but he slipped into the crowd and I lost him.

grounded_facts: A final emotional encounter between Darkman and Julie inside a construction elevator at street level, where they confront the impossibility of their past relationship.
memories.memory_text: I was with Darkman in the elevator at street level, and I reached out to touch his shoulder, then held his charred hand even though it repulsed me—I knew it was him and I chased after him when he left, but he disappeared into the crowd.

grounded_facts: Peyton is ambushed and physically assaulted by Durant and his men in the lab, initiating a violent interrogation.

grounded_facts: A terrifying encounter between Rick and Darkman that unfolds under Rick's bed after Rick is dragged there.

grounded_facts: Darkman peels off his bandages to expose his burnt, grotesque mouth to Rick.

grounded_facts: Darkman tells Rick, 'You always knew there was something like me under the bed,' confirming his monstrous presence.
memories.memory_text: I told Rick, 'You always knew there was something like me under the bed,' confirming my monstrous presence.

memories.memory_text: I smashed my fists around Rick's head, cracking the wall and making plaster fly, leaving him bleeding and broken, teetering on the edge of sanity.

grounded_facts: Darkman, standing among stone gargoyles, vocalizes self-reproach, indicating a moment of emotional distress or moral reflection.
memories.memory_text: I stood among the stone gargoyles and said, 'I've been bad,' hearing my own voice echo with the weight of what I've done.

memories.memory_text: I reached out and gently touched Julie's hair with my clawed hand, a distorted echo of how I once touched her when I was still whole.

memories.memory_text: I entered Julie's apartment at night and stood over her while she slept, a deformed shadow watching her — I reached out and gently touched her hair, remembering how it once was, though now everything feels twisted and fragile.

grounded_facts: Darkman whispers to sleeping Julie, declaring 'I need you,' revealing his emotional dependence and inner turmoil.

memories.memory_text: I spoke to the photo of Peyton and Julie, telling them how desperately I need to reclaim my former face and who I really am.

grounded_facts: Darkman tries to erase burn marks from a photograph of Peyton and Julie, symbolically attempting to reclaim his lost identity.
memories.memory_text: I tried to brush away the burn marks on my face in the photograph of Peyton and Julie, as if erasing them could restore who I once was.

grounded_facts: Julie suddenly sits up in bed, crying out 'Peyton' after dreaming, possibly influenced by Darkman's presence or subconscious connection.
memories.memory_text: I was there when Julie suddenly sat up in bed and cried out 'Peyton' in her dream, and I wondered if my presence had stirred something in her.

memories.memory_text: I stood up to greet them, introduced myself as their legal representative, and right away Mr. Strack Sr. dismissed me—saying he didn’t want 'some fancy-ass woman' handling his negotiations.
I said 'we're only missing one element here' and then calmly named what they weren't — an interested party — watching Strack Jr. almost smile across the table.
I paused, then laid it out — 'Location. Location. And... location.' — making it clear their price had no basis in the actual value of the riverfront land.
I brushed against the steward by accident as we were leaving—just a brief moment, a few quiet words—nothing more.
I stepped out of the cab into the cold night, the lab’s dark outline looming ahead—I walked through the front door alone, the weight of what I was doing pressing on me.
I stepped back and suddenly a beam of light snapped on, then the windows sealed shut with a crash — I couldn’t see outside anymore, and a voice told me to sit down. I just... sat.

I was going over the papers on the bed when the sunlight hit my shoulder, and the more I read, the heavier my chest felt—those memos from Strack to Bellasarious, payments to the zoning commission... they weren’t just irregular, they were wrong.

I called Dale Gorson right then, my voice steady but quiet, telling him I found something I wasn’t meant to see—and I made the choice to reach out to Strack’s son first, not because it was easiest, but because it felt like the right thing to do.

Peyton ran up behind me on the street and just blurted out a marriage proposal—no ring, no warning—while I was already stepping into a cab, and I froze, half in, half out, my mind racing about my career, our life, everything suddenly colliding at once.

I told him I loved him but wasn't ready, closed the cab door, and through the window watched him shrink in the distance, my heart pulling me back even as the cab pulled me away—then I looked again, one last time, but he was already just a dot, gone.

I remember sitting across from Strack, my voice hesitating as I brought up the memo—his father’s signature on it, those payments to the zoning commission. When he called them bribes outright, I could only say I’d already guessed, but it still made my chest tighten.
I recognized the song—'I'm Afraid'—playing from the elevator speakers, and it hit me like a weight, slow and heavy, the way it ached in my chest.
I heard one of the women say, 'He was a rare one,' and the other murmured about not giving up on someone who truly loves you—those words settled deep, like they weren't just about strangers.
I stood at the payphone, light hitting my face, heart pounding as I waited for Peyton to pick up—I whispered, 'please be there Peyton,' like a plea I couldn't hold back anymore.
I was thrown hard onto the sidewalk by the force of the explosion—I didn’t see it coming, just the blast slamming into me and the ground rushing up.
Through the smoke and falling debris, I looked up and saw something burning in the sky—falling fast—Peyton, his body on fire, plummeting like a comet.
I pulled myself up from the ground, dazed, with forks and spoons raining down around me while Peyton’s building burned in the distance like a haystack set aflame.

I didn’t move, but everything else changed—the fire faded, the sky lightened, and the burning paper drifting past turned into leaves; I looked down and saw my suit had become black, like something meant for a funeral.
I saw the marker—'Peyton Westlake'—and buttoned my coat. I straightened up and started walking toward the car.
I was walking, then suddenly I couldn't—grief hit me like a wave. I stumbled, fell to the ground sobbing, clutching the grass, tears streaming down my face until someone helped me up.
A hideous hand, scarred and skeletal, grabbed my shoulder—tendons and bone poking through filthy bandages—and I gasped, stumbling back, rain soaking through my coat as I tried to pull away.
I heard a guttural rasp—'It's meeeeeee'—and froze for a second; the voice was monstrous, but something in those words made my fear twist with pity before I turned and ran into the rain.
I felt his hand crawl up my thigh while I was just trying to sit alone with a drink, and I had to tell him to remove it—then Strack appeared and made him leave.
Strack took me by the arm and led me across the floor. He asked if I'd made a decision about the Belasarius Memorandum. I told him the decision was already made—the papers were destroyed in the fire.
I felt something cold touch my hair, and a whisper—'I need you'—so close it made my skin crawl, but I couldn't wake fully, trapped between dream and fear.
I woke with a jolt, heart racing, calling out for Peyton—his name was on my lips—but the room was empty, just the curtains moving in the wind.

I remember setting down my drink and asking Louis if he’d ever been married, and when he told me about losing her in a plane crash, I felt something shift between us—like we were no longer just two people talking, but two people who had both known real loss.

I was placing flowers on Peyton's marker, my eyes full of tears, when I heard someone say my name—I turned and saw him standing there, whole and smiling, and for a second I couldn't move, couldn't breathe—then everything went black.
I woke to Peyton gently slapping my face. I whispered his name, then told him to hold me and never let me go. He stood, said he was sorry, and walked away quickly with his hand over his face.
I reached for Peyton's hand across the table, my fingers closing around his—my skin touching his, or what felt like skin, but there was something off in the texture, subtle but wrong.

He asked me what I'd do if he were burned so badly I couldn't bear to look at him or let him touch me—his voice serious, almost testing me—and I didn't understand why he'd say that, not when he's right here, seemingly unharmed.
I saw him—rushing through the alley, furtive and quick, unlocking the warehouse door like he was hiding from the world. The way he moved… it wasn’t just secrecy, it was pain.

I touched his face—what was left of it—hanging there from a hook, eyeless and trembling in my hand, the skin sizzling with blisters, and I couldn't scream at first, just froze in horror before the revulsion turned to heartbreak.

After knocking the computer to the floor, shouting that he should've come to me, I finally stopped fighting it—my voice broke, and I told him I would have helped, that I love him no matter what he's become, and meant it with everything.
I told Louis I couldn't see him anymore, and he didn't say much—just set down his drink and said we should talk.

When I told him Peyton was alive and burned, Louis froze — his hand stopped mid-air as he set down the glass, and I saw something shift in his face, like fear or recognition, not surprise but calculation.

I'm standing on the edge of a steel beam, wind tearing at my clothes, clinging to a metal rod—Strack pushed me out here, using me like bait, and then I heard Louis's voice, raw and desperate, calling my name.

I saw Strack reach over and rip Louis's face off—just tear it away with a sickening sound—and then it tumbled down, flapping like paper in the wind before impaling on a steel spike below; I couldn't move, couldn't look away.
I reached for his hand, the charred fingers curled like claws, and forced myself to close my fingers around them—his skin cracked and lifeless, but I held on, afraid he’d vanish if I didn’t.
I ran through the snow, spinning strangers around, searching each face—hoping to see him, terrified I’d miss him in the crowd, knowing he was there but slipping away again.

memories.memory_text: I saw Yakitito's nose take shape in the bio-press, the pins rising perfectly under the wet synthetic layer—smooth, no bunching. For the first time, it looked exactly like his face.

I leaned into the microscope, watching the cells on screen—then saw the numbers flicker. Ninety-eight minutes. Something was wrong. I remember thinking, 'Not again,' before the cells started breaking apart.
I threw the basketball to Yakitito right after he kept punching the wall, shouting about failing—his hands were shaking, and I just needed to break that spiral before it took him under.
He caught the ball after the last answer, blinked, and said it worked every time.
I saw the cells still pulsing through the microscope — they made it to 100 minutes, alive and holding. I gripped the table, my voice breaking as I said, 'The cells are holding, Yakitito.'
Yakitito kept pressing me about asking her to marry me, and when he said 'Maybe I ask to marry you,' I froze — all I could say was that her father wouldn't approve.
I watched Julie sleeping, my shadow falling across her face... I reached out and brushed her hair, just once, softly.

I remember standing there, blurting it out—'Julie, I'm asking you to marry me'—without a ring, without anything, just needing her to know I realized how much she meant, but she was already pulling away.
I told Yakitito I asked Julie, and she said 'I don't know'. I stood and stretched after saying it, just as the phone rang.
I hear Julie’s voice cracking through the phone line, desperate—'please be there Peyton'—and my hand tightens around the receiver, my breath catching in my throat.
I remember the sudden grip on my wrist, the voice saying 'Don't bother'—then the lights snapping on one by one, revealing all of them, surrounding me.
Pauly's fist came out of nowhere—I saw it launching toward me, then everything exploded in pain as I crashed into the table, glass flying everywhere.
I felt the spark catch when the bird’s beak hit the button—I saw the flash in my eyes, that blue light blooming behind my eyelids before the world went silent.
I remember flying—my body just torn loose, spinning through the air like a doll, and then nothing but the sky and that endless silence before the sound finally ripped through me.
I remember falling—flames tearing at me, the sky spinning, then nothing but fire as I crashed down.
I hit the water hard, flames still clinging to me, the shock of the cold and fire burning at the same time—I couldn't scream, just gasp as the river swallowed the fire.
I groaned as I sank beneath the murky water, flaming debris from the building falling around me.
I felt the needle go into my knee—no pain, just pressure, like something pressing through thick cloth—but I couldn’t move, couldn’t speak, just listened as they talked about me like I wasn’t there.
I staggered across the street toward her, my body aching, rain mixing with the mud on my face—I saw Julie step out and open her umbrella, and for a second, I thought she might recognize me.
I reached out, then pulled my hand back when I saw her flinch—my voice cracked through the bandages, 'It's meeeeeee,' but she was already stepping away, her hand at her throat, not knowing it was me.
I saw it spinning in the drain, just a scrap caught in the whirlpool of rain—my own face staring up from the paper, the headline saying I was dead.
I picked up that photo from the ashes—me and Julie, smiling, whole—and I couldn't breathe. I asked her if she could still love this... thing I've become, knowing she'd never look at me the same.
I saw the glint of Durant's lighter in the ash—twisted, scorched, but still there—and something inside me snapped. Rage surged up, raw and hot, like something feral waking in my chest.

I remember the photo—burned, barely there—just enough to see Julie laughing on my shoulder, my face half-hidden. I punched the data in anyway, whispering, 'This'll have to do,' knowing it wasn't clear, but it was all I had.
I saw her place flowers on my marker, and when she turned and saw me—alive, whole—I tried to smile, but she just stared and then collapsed. I didn’t expect her to faint.
I felt the sun burning my cheek, then saw the blister form and smoke—I covered it and ran before she could see.

I asked Julie, my voice tight, what if I was burned so badly she couldn't stand to look at me—couldn't stand my touch. My hand trembled under hers, synthetic skin buzzing with the effort to stay still.
I shoved the pink elephant at Julie, my voice raw, telling her to take it—just take it—while my face burned and the skin split open, smoke curling off my cheek.
The rage faded and I saw her—really saw her—frozen, terrified, and I barely whispered 'Forgive me' before running, the elephant still clutched under my arm like I didn’t even know it was there.
I felt her hand lift my face—cold, trembling—then drop me when the skin sizzled and the flies buzzed. I couldn’t speak, couldn’t move. Just dangled there, hearing her scream.
I heard Julie scream my name—'Peyton!!'—from outside, her voice cracking with fear, and I froze, my breath catching in my throat as the engines roared closer.

I felt the rivets tear through my wrists, pinning me to the beam, and then the rage—hot and blinding—flooded in, and I saw Strack laughing, Julie in his arms, his face burning into coins, my face melting off like wax.
I turned my face toward her, let her see the scars—those twisted remains—and then I told her to take my hand. I felt her hesitate, but she did it, she put her hand in mine.
I told her I’ve changed inside, that Peyton is gone—that what we had belonged in the light, and I can’t go back. Then I walked away, pulled on the mask, and vanished into the crowd.
